info.name: Activityual API
info.description:
Postman collection for the Activityual gateway. One folder per backend service.

Quick start:
1. Set the `base` variable (defaults to http://localhost:8080).
2. Run Auth > Register once, then Auth > Login. The login test script stashes accessToken, refreshToken and userId into collection variables so the rest of the requests just work.
3. Run Activities > Create. The test script copies the returned id into activityId.
4. From there log a few entries under Tracking and poke around Analytics, Coach, Recommendations and Notifications.

variable.description: Gateway URL. Local docker-compose runs on 8080. In cloud, point this at the ALB / CloudFront API domain.
Filled in by the Login request.
Filled in by the Login request.
Filled in by the Login request.
Filled in by Activities > Create. You can also paste one in by hand.
Paste this in after listing recommendations if you want to hit Accept.
Paste this in after listing notifications if you want to mark one read.

item.name: Auth (auth-service, port 8081)
item.description: Register, login, refresh, and a small /me endpoint. This is the only service that touches authdb. Passwords get bcrypt-hashed on the way in. Login returns a 30 minute access token and a 7 day refresh token.

request.description: Sign up a new user. Same response shape as Login so the frontend can drop you straight onto the dashboard. Returns 409 if the email is already taken, 400 if validation fails.

exec: console.log('Saved accessToken and userId to collection vars');

request.description: Logs in and returns an access + refresh token pair. The test script writes both tokens and the userId into collection variables, so every other request in here picks them up automatically.
Swap a valid refresh token for a new access + refresh pair. Returns 401 if the refresh token has expired or been revoked.
Returns the current user's profile. The frontend uses this to render the avatar and name in the navbar.

item.name: Activities (activity-service, port 8082)
item.description: CRUD on the user's activity catalogue, i.e. the list of habits you want to track. Rows live in activitydb.activities, scoped to the JWT user. Frequency is one of DAILY, WEEKLY_3, WEEKLY_5, WEEKLY_7, CUSTOM.

request.description: Add a new activity to track. Returns the saved row including the generated id. The test script writes that id into {{activityId}} so the rest of the requests can use it.
All activities belonging to the current user. Used by the /activities page and to populate dropdowns elsewhere.
Fetch a single activity. 404 if it doesn't exist or belongs to a different user.
Edit title, category, frequency or notes on an existing activity.
Soft-deletes the activity. Analytics keeps the history so old streaks and charts don't break.

item.name: Tracking (tracking-service, port 8083)
item.description: Where you actually log progress. This is the one service that publishes the activity.logged event to RabbitMQ, and it does it through a transactional outbox so a log can never be saved without the event going out (or vice versa).

request.description: Mark today's entry as done, missed or completed. Under the hood this writes one row to trackingdb.activity_logs and one row to trackingdb.outbox_events in the same transaction. A scheduled relay picks up the outbox row a couple of seconds later and publishes to the activity.events topic exchange. Four services consume it: analytics recomputes streaks, coach embeds the log into Chroma, recommendation recomputes nudges, notification drops a row in the inbox.
Activities due today that haven't been ticked off yet. Backs the 'due today' widget on the dashboard.
Same idea as due-today but for a rolling 7 day window.
Most recent log entries, newest first. Powers the timeline strip on the dashboard.

item.name: Analytics (analytics-service, port 8084)
item.description: Read-only aggregates built from activity.logged events. Stored as denormalised fact tables in analyticsdb so the dashboard reads stay cheap.

request.description: Everything the dashboard needs in one call: total logs, done count, missed count, consistency percentage, and the most and least consistent activities.
Current and longest streak per activity.

item.name: Coach (coach-service, port 8085)
item.description: The AI coach. Every log gets embedded into Chroma. When you ask a question it pulls back the most relevant chunks of your own history, builds a grounded prompt, and calls Ollama (llama3.2:3b) for the answer.

request.description:
Ask the coach a free-form question. Response shape is { answer, chunks: [{ text, timestamp, score }] }. The frontend shows the chunks next to the answer so you can see it is grounded in your actual logs instead of made up.

Things worth trying:
- Why do I keep missing my workout?
- What's my most consistent habit this month?
- Give me a plan to improve my reading streak.

item.name: Recommendations (recommendation-service, port 8086)
item.description: Suggestions about when and how often to do each activity. These are plain SQL heuristics over the user's log history, recomputed every time an activity.logged event comes in.

request.description: All current recommendations for the user. Each one has a confidence score; the UI hides anything below 0.6 so you don't get noise.
Force a recompute for one activity instead of waiting for the next event. Mostly useful when demoing or debugging.
Mark a recommendation as accepted or rejected. We keep this so later on we can check whether accepted nudges actually improve completion rates.
A day-of-week by time-of-day grid with completion rate per cell. The /recommendations page uses it to render the heatmap chart.

item.name: Notifications (notification-service, port 8087)
item.description: In-app inbox. Pure consumer; every activity.logged event ends up as a row in notifdb.notifications.

request.description: Notifications for the user, newest first, with an unread count for the badge.
Mark one notification as read.
